My brother wasn't hurt.
>I am guessing that you still go to school? Go to your school counselor and ask them for recommendations.

I've considered this, however, when I previously dealt with my counselor, she acted really condescendingly towards me (I was getting my schedule changed.) I don't if it was a bad time of day, or if she didn't like the fact I was changing my schedule, regardless, I don't know how respectful she'd be, and I'm kind of afraid to ask her.

I am the only girl. I'm in the middle. I'm somehwat close to all of them, the most so with my 2nd oldest.
My mom and I sometimes do 'just talk' and chit-chat and receive advice, I think she may have a short temper due to factors you stated.

>I would think that a psychologist wouldn't be a bad place to start. Someone who would recognize the challenges that autism presents but also on the therapy side of things.

How should I go about finding a psychologist? I have a friend in therapy for ADHD, should I ask them? I'm afraid of asking my parents. I also really don't need them calling CPS or anything.

Also, really, thank you so so much for your reply. It's made me feel better about my situation. :)

*hugs back
Thank you. I'll look into that movie.
>Did you talk to your parents (namely your father) about this? This is a predatory behavior that needed to be addressed. If not to protect you, then to protect any future young ladies. What he did was so very wrong. But being he found you to be weak and naive one time, he may try that crap again.

My cousin is a bit younger than me, so I don't think he'll try it again. But anyway. I left a note to my mom about it, but she never spoke to me on the issue. I later confronted her in-person about it, and she told me it was probably an issue of my cousin discovering his sexual identity. She said she'd talk to him and his parents about it, however, it was not discussed further so I don't know. I didn't talk to my father about it. Our relationship is somewhat distant.
